pass_a_gloss: Who, having counted up such things, will not call out that apostolic word, that not worthy are the sufferings of the now time toward the glory about to be uncovered into us? For how is not the confession in front of the father much bigger than the confession in front of humans? And how is not the confession in the heavens of the one confessed exceeding by excess the confession on earth, which the witnesses confess, the son of God? And someone having counted to deny in front of the humans, let him be reminded of the one who spoke without falsehood: I also will deny him in front of my father in the heavens. And since Matthew wrote up, I also will confess in him in front of my father in the heavens, and Luke, and the son of the human will confess in him in front of the messengers of God, I set my mind on it, whether perhaps the firstborn of every creation, the likeness of the unseen God, confesses the one who confessed, in front of the father in the heavens, and the one having come to be out of seed of David by flesh, and through this happening to be son of a human, and having come to be out of a woman, she herself also being a human, and through this being styled son of a human, as the human belonging to Jesus is thought of, confesses the ones who confessed in front of the messengers of God. And the matching thing must be rendered also about the ones who denied. And still this also must be looked at, that the one confessing in the son in front of the humans sets forward, as much as is on himself, Christianity and the father of this Christianity before those at whose hands he confesses; and the one confessed by the firstborn of every creation and the son of the human is set forward through the confession of the son of God and the son of the human to the father in the heavens and to the messengers of God. And if indeed not the one setting forward himself, that one is tested and true, but whom the lord sets forward, how is it not needful to think tested and true the one judged worthy of the setting forward toward the father in the heavens and toward the messengers of God? And if this one is tested and true, and the ones near to him, whom as gold in a melting pot by the tortures and the questionings the lord tested, and as a whole fruit offering of sacrifice received, what is it needful to say about the ones shown up in the oven of trial and having denied, whom as untested he denies in front of the father in the heavens and in the sight of the messengers of God, denying the one worthy of denial?
pass_b_english: Who, reckoning such things, will not utter that saying of the apostle: “The sufferings of the present time are not worth comparing with the glory that is to be revealed to us” (Romans 8:18)? For how is the confession before the Father not far greater than the confession before men? And how does the confession in heaven made by the one who was confessed not surpass beyond all measure the confession on earth, by which the martyrs confess the Son of God? But let anyone who reckons on denying “before men” remember the one who said, and does not lie, “I too will deny him before my Father who is in heaven” (Matthew 10:33).

Since Matthew wrote, “I too will confess in him before my Father who is in heaven” (Matthew 10:32), and Luke, “The Son of Man too will confess in him before the angels of God” (Luke 12:8), I pause over this: perhaps the “firstborn of all creation”, the “image of the invisible God” (Colossians 1:15), confesses the one who has confessed, before the Father in heaven; while he who came “from the seed of David according to the flesh” (Romans 1:3), and for that reason is “Son of Man”, who was born of a woman, she too being human, and for that reason is called “Son of Man”, which is how the man in Jesus is understood, confesses those who have confessed “before the angels of God”. A corresponding account must also be given of those who have denied.

We must consider this further. The one who confesses in the Son “before men” commends, as far as lies in him, Christianity and the Father of this Christianity before those in whose presence he confesses; while the one who is confessed by the firstborn of all creation and by the Son of Man is commended, through the confession of the Son of God and of the Son of Man, to the Father in heaven and to the angels of God. And if indeed “it is not the one who commends himself who is approved, but the one whom the Lord commends” (2 Corinthians 10:18), how can we fail to hold that the one judged worthy to be commended to the Father in heaven and to the angels of God is approved? And if he is approved, and those like him, whom the Lord has tested “like gold in a furnace” by tortures and interrogations “and accepted like the whole burnt offering of a sacrifice” (Wisdom of Solomon 3:6), what must we say of those who were exposed in the furnace of temptation and denied, whom he denies as unapproved before the Father in heaven and “before the angels of God” (Luke 12:9), denying the one who deserves denial?

choices.choice: 2026-11-11: retranslated in full from Koetschau (GCS 2, ch. 35); the old English was a digest. It turned Origen's questions into a call to confess, invented 'Abraham's seed' and a 'furnace of humiliation', and dropped Romans 8:18, the contrast of earthly and heavenly confession, 2 Corinthians 10:18 and Wisdom of Solomon 3:6.

Read μείξων as μείζων, ἔμπροσHev as ἔμπροσθεν, 9500 as θεοῦ, νεἰκὼν as εἰκών, Javid as Δαβίδ, &x as ἐκ, χριστιανιομὸν as χριστιανισμόν, αὐτὸν as αὑτόν (Koetschau's apparatus: M αὑτόν), doxıuos as δόκιμος, ag χρυσὸν ἐν xwvevrnoim as ὡς χρυσὸν ἐν χωνευτηρίῳ, τοῖ as τοῦ.
Kept as Origen's hedge: 'I pause over this: perhaps ...'; the two-level reading of confession is offered as a question, not asserted.
'the man in Jesus', i.e. the human being Jesus was; no further theological gloss added.
